title: Kombu
summary: The kombu is a C-shaped brass horn of southern India. A narrow mouthpiece opens along a curved tube into a flaring bell, and by tightening the lips the player sounds a handful of notes of the overtone series: a bold, bright call.
howToPlay: Five notes of the horn are lit along the tube, the higher ones nearer the mouthpiece.
A band of breath runs from the mouth to the note you strike, and rings of sound leave the bell.
Long notes swell slowly: strike close to the beat and let them ring.
rules: A call is a line of long notes, each struck close to its beat.
Long notes swell slowly: strike on the beat and let them ring.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: Its calls open processions and festivals, and are played in pairs with drums and pipes.
credits: Tradition: the kombu; calls written for this game
